description: Somos un equipo de cinco estudiantes apasionados por la tecnología, la inteligencia artificial, el análisis de datos y la exploración espacial. Contamos con experiencia trabajando con Python, Machine Learning, análisis y visualización de datos, y queremos utilizar estas habilidades para desarrollar una solución con datos reales de NASA que pueda abordar un problema ambiental.
summary: PyroTrace is an open-source web platform that turns 25 years of NASA FIRMS active-fire detections into one comparable record for the seven countries of Central America. MODIS has observed fires since 2000, and VIIRS since 2012, but VIIRS detects many more small fires, so simply adding both records makes every year after 2012 look like it had several times more fire. We built a four-stage harmonization method in DuckDB SQL that keeps every original detection and assigns it a weight in VIIRS-equivalent units: MODIS detections already seen by VIIRS count as zero, and the rest receive country- and time-specific factors. Applied to 3.6 million detections, it reduces the jump at the sensor transition from 6.4 times to 1.6 times. Users can explore the result in an interactive map, a historical calendar, and a statistics panel that compares any month or year with its historical range, switching between raw counts and the harmonized index and downloading the data as CSV. This helps students, researchers, and fire-prevention teams recognize real patterns and critical seasons instead of sensor artifacts.
details:
What it does

 PyroTrace is an open-source web platform that turns NASA FIRMS active-fire detections into one consistent, comparable record for the seven countries of Central America (Belize, Costa Rica, El Salvador,
 Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Panama), from November 2000 to the present. MODIS has observed fires since 2000 and VIIRS since 2012, but VIIRS detects many more small fires. If both records are simply added together, every
 year after 2012 appears to have several times more fire than the years before it. PyroTrace corrects this so that users can compare any period with confidence.

 How it works

 1. Two-part FIRMS ingestion: Because NASA FIRMS only consolidates detections into annual country archive CSVs roughly one year in the past, a Python pipeline downloads the historical country archives (3,621,309 detections from
 November 2000 through December 2025) and stores them as local Parquet files.
 2. DuckDB CLI processing & four-stage harmonization: Using the DuckDB CLI, the pipeline fuses the Parquet files, runs a four-stage SQL harmonization method that keeps every original detection and adds a weight in VIIRS-equivalent
 units, and normalizes the result into a star schema. It computes the local solar time of each detection, matches MODIS and VIIRS detections of the same fire (within 2.2 km and one hour, searching neighboring cells so grid edges do
 not split matches), estimates country-specific calibration factors from the 2012+ overlap period, and assigns the final weights. VIIRS weights are divided by the number of active VIIRS satellites, so adding a new satellite does not
 inflate the record.
 3. PostGIS storage, clustering & API: The harmonized star schema is bulk-loaded via DuckDB into PostgreSQL/PostGIS, grouped into spatiotemporal fire events (0.02° cells with 24-hour continuity, centroids, and 400 m buffered convex-
 hull perimeters), and published through a FastAPI backend with about 50 documented endpoints.
 4. Near-real-time (NRT) worker: Because true real-time satellite fire monitoring does not exist due to orbital overpass and processing latency, a containerized worker bridges recent dates in near-real-time using two Area API
 phases: a quota-aware 5-day catch-up backfill and 5-minute NRT polling across MODIS, Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21. New detections are labeled as provisional until harmonized and distributed as NRT notifications via NATS
 JetStream.
 5. Web application: A Vue 3 web application queries the API directly to filter detections and generate statistics: an interactive map with date, sensor, and drawn-area filters; a historical calendar; a statistics panel that
 compares each month and year with its historical range; and a landing page that explains the sensors and the method in plain language.

 Results

 Between 2011 and 2013, raw detections increase 6.4x (6.41x) because VIIRS started observing; with our harmonized index, the change is 1.6x (1.57x). We also report a residual step of about 37% after 2012 and explain how we plan to
 remove it, because we believe transparent limitations are part of good science.

 Benefits and intended impact

 PyroTrace is free, requires no account, and does not need geospatial skills. It helps students and teachers learn about satellite fire observation, gives researchers a documented regional record with CSV downloads, and helps
 environmental analysts, protected-area managers, and firefighters recognize patterns, anomalies, and critical fire seasons when planning prevention. Because the pipeline is driven by FIRMS country files, the same method can be
 extended to other regions.

 Tools and technologies

 • Languages: Python, SQL, TypeScript.
 • Data: NASA FIRMS (MODIS and VIIRS active fires, country archive and Area API), NASA POWER, Natural Earth, Esri World Imagery.
 • Processing and storage: DuckDB (CLI, spatial and PostgreSQL extensions), Apache Parquet, SQLite, PostgreSQL with PostGIS.
 • Backend & analytics: FastAPI, SQLModel, NATS JetStream, NumPy, Shapely (statistical anomaly comparisons, geometric fire-event movement/expansion metrics, and spatial buffering).
 • Frontend: Vue 3, Vite, Pinia, MapLibre GL, ECharts, Tailwind CSS.
 • Operations: Podman Compose, Caddy, and a Microsoft Azure virtual machine (Standard_B2as_v2, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, 30 GB Premium_LRS, northcentralus).
 • Documentation: Typst.
 • AI assistance: Claude, ChatGPT, and Google Antigravity helped with coding, debugging, analysis, and writing; every output was reviewed and tested by the team.

 What makes it creative

 Instead of replacing the data with a new grid, we keep every original detection and express the harmonization as a weight per point. This makes the method fully traceable: each number on the screen can be traced back to a real
 FIRMS detection. The interface lets users switch between raw counts and the harmonized index, so they can see the sensor effect with their own eyes. We also built honest statistics: partial months and near-real-time data are marked
 and excluded from historical comparisons, so incomplete data never looks like high or low fire activity.

 Factors we considered

 Scientific accuracy (a detection is a hot pixel, not an individual fire, and missing detections can mean clouds or no satellite overpass); differences between satellites and observation times; reproducibility, with synthetic tests
 that run the production SQL; performance, processing millions of records on a single machine; accessibility for non-experts, with plain-language explanations; and openness, publishing the full code, data sources, and technical
 reports.

 Technical Reports

 • English Report (PDF): https://github.com/vect-maker/modis-viirs-harmonization/blob/main/apps/report/output/report.pdf
 • Spanish Report (PDF): https://github.com/vect-maker/modis-viirs-harmonization/blob/main/apps/report/output/report-es.pdf
